chunks: And regarding the forearm, if it breaks and is then set without a defect or flaw, its blood-money is one-third of the blood-money of the soul, being three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar. So if one of the two bones of the forearm breaks, its blood-money is one-fifth of the blood-money of the hand, being one hundred dinars. So if both bones of the forearm break, its blood-money is one-fifth of the blood-money of the hand, being one hundred dinars.

And regarding the break of one of the two radius/ulna bones, it is fifty dinars, and regarding both of them is one hundred dinars. So if one of the two bones cracks, regarding it is four-fifths of the blood-money of one of the two bones of the forearm, being forty dinars; and the blood-money for its exposure is a quarter of the blood-money of its break, being twenty-five dinars; and the blood-money of the displacement of its bones is a quarter of the blood-money of its break, being twenty-five dinars; and the blood-money of its piercing is half the blood-money of its exposure, being twelve dinars and half a dinar; and the blood-money of its being jabbed is fifty dinars.

So if there is in it a wound that does not heal, its blood-money is one-third of the blood-money of the forearm, being thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar, and that is one-third of the blood-money of that which is in it.

key_terms.الزَّنْدَانِ: The two wrist bones (radius and ulna)

ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for a broken forearm or wrist in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This passage from al-Kafi elaborates on the detailed jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) for injuries to the forearm (*sa'id*) and wrist (*zand*), categorizing damages by fracture, exposure, and chronicity. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of precise quantification, linking specific limb injuries to fractions of the total *diyah* of the soul or the hand, thereby ensuring equitable compensation in legal disputes.

en.hubeali: And regarding the forearm, when it breaks, then is bandaged upon and there is no fault, so its wergild is one-third of a wergild of the soul, being three hundred and thirty three Dinars and one-third of a Dinar. So if one of the two bones of the forearm breaks, its wergild is a fifth of the wergild of the hand, being one hundred Dinars. So if both the bones of the forearm were to break, its wergild is (still) a fifth of the wergild of the hand, being one hundred Dinars.

And regarding the breaking of one of the two wrists, it is fifty Dinars, and regarding both of these is one hundred Dinars. So if one of the two bones cracks, so regarding it is four-fifths of the wergild of one of the two bones of the forearms, being forty Dinars; and the wergild for its exposure is a quarter of the wergild of its breaking, being twenty five Dinars; and wergild of the displacement of its bones is a quarter of the wergild of its breaking, being twenty five Dinars; and the wergild of its piercing is half the wergild of its exposure, being twelve Dinars and half a Dinar; and wergild of its being jabbed is fifty Dinars.

So if there was a scar in it which does not get cured, so its wergild is one-third of the wergild of the forearm, being thirty-three Dinars, and one-third of a Dinar, that is one-third of the wergild of that which is in it’.
